references.text: The preceding context regarding the borrowing of animals and liability when the owner is not present, establishing principles for compensation in cases of damage or death to borrowed animals.
The following verse addressing the situation when the owner is present, illustrating the contrast in the distribution of responsibility.
Laws concerning restitution and repayment when one has acted dishonestly with a neighbor's property, including the principle of full compensation.
Laws regarding liability for a neighbor's property and the duty to care for what belongs to others.
Laws on liability for compensation when someone's animal is injured or killed, establishing principles for restitution.
Complementary rules in the Mosaic Law that together form a comprehensive picture of responsibility and the obligation to compensate for damage to another's property.
A direct parallel confirming the general law of full compensation for killed animals regardless of how the damage occurred.
A parallel legal structure where the responsible party pays compensation while the dead animal goes to the one who caused the harm.
A theological contrast that limits the principle of compensation: animal life requires restitution, human life requires a life.
Parallel principles regarding liability when one's animal causes damage to another's property.
